steps.caption: Open More in the sidebar, then Automation.
At the top: 'Automation active' — background checks, research, scoring and updates are running. Pause automation stops them all.
Seven tabs: Overview, Daily plan, History, Background jobs, Weekly review, Budgets & usage and Notifications.
A warning appears when many background jobs are waiting — results that depend on them may be out of date.
The counters: total workflows run, active now, scheduled, completed, failed, delayed, and items that need you.
Total, Completed, Failed and Delayed are links — each opens the History tab filtered to those runs.
System alerts: the most serious first — failed workflows, decisions waiting for you, stale outputs and changed information.
Each alert has a label (Failed, Needs you, Stale, Changed…) and links to where you fix it.
Capacity warnings: today's clashes — overlapping meetings, too many meetings, overdue promises.
Needs attention: failed, paused and waiting jobs, plus records that became out of date. Start here every day.
Each row shows the job, its status chip (Failed, Paused…), how far it got and the error in plain words.
Running now lists jobs in progress. Empty means nothing is working in the background right now.
Start a job: run a workflow yourself — here, prepare tomorrow's meetings and list open commitments.
Scheduled: the daily plan at 08:00 and the weekly review on Friday, with their next run.
All workflows: each one, whether it is On or Paused, what starts it and how many steps it has.
For example: 'Reassess after requirement change' runs by itself whenever a client's requirement changes.
Recently finished: the last jobs and how they ended (Done, Partly done, Failed, Cancelled).
Connections: when mail or calendar last worked. A broken connection is shown here — never hidden.
Usage and limits, per resource: research, contact enrichment, transcription and AI — used, limit and remaining.
Open a workflow to see exactly what it does.
What it does, what starts it, when it last ran and when it runs next.
Steps in order. 'After: …' means a step waits for an earlier one; steps without it run in parallel.
Controls: Pause workflow stops new runs of this one workflow. Priority decides which job goes first (admins only).
Recent runs, the records the last run touched and the change history are further down. Export log downloads a run's history.
